title: Adic formal completion and its completed affine charts
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent ideal. An adic formal completion presentation is the pair $(X,I)$. For another quasi-coherent ideal $J$, define its completed closed subspace as the colimit, in ringed spaces, of the closed subschemes cut out by $I^{n+1}+J$, with their closed-immersion transition maps. Thus its structure sheaf is the inverse limit of the thickening structure sheaves. The formal completion $\widehat X_I$ is the case $J=0$, with its canonical map to $X$. On an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the completed chart ring is $\widehat B_{I(U)}=\varprojlim_n B/I(U)^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and the extended ideal of $J$ is $J(U)\widehat B$. The chart ideal is $I(U)\widehat B$. The reduced closed fibre is the closed subscheme defined by $\sqrt I$. Define $\operatorname{Spf}(A,K)$ by the same ringed-space colimit for $(\operatorname{Spec}A,\widetilde K)$. A formal chart over $U$ is the inverse image of $U$ under the canonical map. A Noetherian adic formal space is a ringed space admitting a finite open cover by $\operatorname{Spf}(A_i,K_i)$ with $A_i$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $K_i$ finitely generated, and $A_i$ complete and separated for powers of $K_i$. Empty finite covers are permitted. All these are constructions or predicates, with no chart-comparison theorem built into the presentation.
